0.content:
Chuychu was Cusco's daughter and Chasca's adoptive younger sister. As a child she resented how Chasca's fights consumed their parents and cost her friends. Once she blurted out "You're the worst vulture here!" and Chasca fled into the wild. Chuychu then learned the fight had started because other children insulted their family, and that adults had told them not to play with Chuychu in case her sister's "sickness" was contagious. She searched the mountains, found Chasca collapsed with shattered hands, burned her own hands lighting a fire, and brought her "home". As adults they argued constantly, Chuychu nagging Chasca not to rush headlong into danger. Chuychu became an expert in treating Abyssal corruption. In 5.1, during the Abyss invasion, monsters ambushed the sisters on the way to the Stadium of the Sacred Flame and Chuychu was contaminated. The Traveler purified her, but too late. Chuychu said she had never understood what Chasca lived with, told her to "spread your wings and fly free", and said she was the sister she was proud of. Then she died.

Earlier in 5.0, Chuychu confronted Chasca at the Scions of the Canopy over her plan to enter the Night Kingdom. Chasca asked whether this was "one of our normal arguments, or a serious one", and Chuychu gave her blessing. In 5.1 Chuychu insisted on joining Chasca to trail a Fatui group and watched the patrols while they spied out the search for the Source Mechanism. Her name is in the Record Penned by All. Their clan chief Mutota later caught himself calling for her help.

Chuychu's spirit reached the Night Kingdom, helped the Traveler there with Saurian aid against Gosoythoth, and appeared to Chasca in a dream, saying she no longer needed to pick fights with her. Chasca insisted the dream was "nothing like her real self". Told later that Chuychu had really helped, she declined to seek her out: Chuychu was "probably sick of nagging her older sister".

1.content:
Chimpu is the pink-plumed Qucusaur who found the abandoned infant Chasca and raised her as her own, always letting her daughters eat first. Coya is Chimpu's daughter, Chasca's Qucusaur "big sister", who always beat her at hide-and-seek. Chasca understands their calls "about nine times out of ten" through sound and body language. When Chimpu sent Chasca back to humans, Coya protested. Years later Coya asked Chasca to leave the tribe and live wild with her; Chasca hesitated, and Coya flew off feeling betrayed.

In the 5.2 Tribal Chronicles a Qucusaur attacking merchants turned out to be Coya: hunters supplying Allpa had stolen her chick Chime. Chimpu, acting as go-between, led Chasca to Coya's island nest near Ochkanatlan. Coya followed them to the flying workshop, rammed Allpa, then shielded Chasca from the relic's blast and collapsed from old injuries; Cusco pronounced her fine. Coya revealed she had already forgiven Chasca once she had a family of her own. Since then Coya is warming slowly to humans, Chime plays with the tribe's children, and Chimpu nags Chasca to build a nest of her own.

Before the final battle in 5.3, Chasca and Coya appeared together to bless the Traveler. Chasca said Coya now understood why she chose human society, love and happiness, and had vowed to protect it, "and I would do the same for her." A Sunspray memory: Chimpu once breathed fire onto fruit Coya brought home to celebrate Chasca's solo win over Abyss monsters.

2.comment: Chasca: Cusco and the human family
2.content:
Cusco agreed to take in an orphan and was handed a child tearing at raw meat: "you didn't say it was an orphaned Qucusaurus!" He saw that her fights had no gain behind them, the mark of the Abyss. When a shaman advised returning her to the forest, he refused: "It's too late now." He and his wife then spent years chasing cures and elders. Chasca credits "Chuychu and her- I mean, our parents" with accepting her and swears to defend their tribe for as long as she lives.

After Chuychu's death Cusco told the Traveler that Chasca had grown more reckless and was skipping the check-ups every three months that they had agreed on; he did not want to lose another daughter. Mavuika visited the grieving parents. Chasca resolved to pull them out of their loneliness while knowing she can never replace Chuychu. During the 5.2 crisis her adoptive mother wrote to Cusco from the Masters of the Night-Wind to scold him for not watching Chasca more closely.

3.content:
Allpa, a Flower-Feather elder and Flying Captain, brought the young Chasca into the tribe and later took on her education. At first Chasca only wondered whether beating the Elder would end the lectures. The second time, Chasca asked to learn ("Teach me. Become strong... Abyss... want to defeat"). Allpa handed her a woven scroll, "Peacemaker - the Art of Communication", and told her language is humanity's greatest weapon.

In 5.2 Phlogiston Wings, jetpacks that let the Wingless fly, reached the clan through merchants working for "Tepal", a failed applicant from the Children of Echoes. The real Tepal was Allpa's son, long dead from his own Phlogiston experiments. Grief-stricken and blaming the Qucusaurs, Allpa had taken his name, drained captive Qucusaurs' glands for stable Phlogiston, and planned to overthrow chief Mutota. Confronted in the flying workshop, she caged Coya's chick as leverage. When the relic went unstable she tried to carry it away and die a hero. Chasca and Coya knocked her clear to deny her that martyrdom. Chasca asked whether she still believed Qucusaurs could not form bonds; Allpa had no answer. She is now jailed in a remnant of the workshop.

4.comment: Chasca: Vuka and the sixth hero
4.content:
Vuka ("Transcension") is the Ancient Name of the Flower-Feather Clan. As Chuychu died, grief tore Abyssal energy out of Chasca in an anguished scream; she reined it back in. The spirit of Menilek, Vuka's bearer in the war five hundred years ago, appeared. He spoke of a life of pain risen above and the epitaph "My life's suffering shall be my epitaph... to remember the pain I endured, and finally, transcended." Chasca repeated the words and became the sixth of Natlan's modern heroes. She then helped Mavuika take up the heroes' strength for the counterattack.

Afterwards she thanked the Traveler, saying that if she had lost control in the wild the counterattack might never have happened. She vowed to rise above her struggle "in the spirit of Vuka" and become the person Chuychu believed in. The first bearer of Vuka was Lianca, founder of the clan.

5.comment: Chasca: The voice of the Abyss within
5.content:
Chasca survived Abyssal contamination as a child, but part of it stayed. It took the form of a voice that first guided her hunting, then urged her to "Fight. Bite. Destroy" whenever people quarrelled, and grew louder the more conflict surrounded her. A shaman said the Abyss had engraved conflict into her soul and that it would worsen with age. Learning to communicate and rely on others weakened it until she thought it gone.

In a Night Warden War it returned as a phantom identical to her, offering power and the understanding no one else gave. It almost won by appealing to her loneliness. The remembered voices of Chuychu, Cusco, Coya and Chimpu stopped her, and she shot it, saying this was the only way to make peace between them. Her Vision appeared in place of a bullet. She tells others that slowing breathing and controlling emotion helps keep corrosion symptoms in check, "speaking from experience".

6.content:
Soulsniper: Ritual Staff is Chasca's oversized flying gun with a revolver cylinder and reins, forged by Xilonen. Chasca gave only a vague idea. Xilonen then spent a whole day interrogating her about her flying routine and filled the floor with discarded designs, and Chasca fell asleep first. Xilonen then made her memorise a maintenance manual. On receiving it Chasca recalled a scroll's line, "a bullet has the most power when it has yet to leave the chamber", and named her calling: "from this day forth, we shall be the 'Peacemakers.'"

Xilonen says it had to stay stable at speed and needed special high-altitude ammunition; Chasca shrugged off the recoil and accuracy problems. Xilonen calls her "a flying ace". During the 5.8 holiday Mualani wanted it turned into a giant water gun; Chasca said Xilonen would never agree.

7.content: Chasca's role is to settle disputes when all else fails, between humans, tribes, humans and Saurians, or Saurians themselves. The Character Stories admit that her eloquence matters less than the fact that she is "ludicrously strong". Faced with her, belligerents find sitting down to talk the best choice, and two chiefs once issued a joint reconciliation statement "drafted entirely of our own free will". Kinich says she silences both parties, who wake up in sickbeds having forgotten the quarrel. Ororon calls it "armed deterrence". Ifa says she "cures a lot of ills that are beyond my reach". She seems to appear wherever conflict starts, like a beast catching the scent of prey. Since the war she has had little work, which she does not mind.

8.comment: Chasca: Kachina and the Night Kingdom rescue
8.content: In the 5.0 Pilgrimage, Chasca led the team (with Iansan, Kaiulani, Kibangu and Kachina) into a Night Warden War. Kachina fell and could not revive, because the Abyss had corrupted the Wayob. Chasca called it partly her fault and refused to leave her there. She took the Traveler and Mualani to Wayna of the Scions of the Canopy for the Spiritspeaker Stone. When the Stone, overwhelmed by the Abyss, threatened the merchant Vichama, she destroyed it. With the Traveler, Mualani and Iansan she entered the Night Kingdom and found Kachina; Mavuika burned her keepsakes to pull them out. Chasca calls Kachina an outstanding warrior whose victory came from long, tireless effort.

9.content: They met as small children and fought over a toy, maybe Mualani's surfboard, Chasca jokes, wanting to hunt on water. Chasca does not remember it, and says no feud with Mualani lasts more than a day. Mualani was surprised the brawler became a Peacemaker. Chasca sums up their friendship: "She talks, I listen, sometimes we spar." She also calls her an extrovert to the core who would not know what to do alone in a corner.

10.comment: Chasca: The flying squad and the Wingless
10.content: The Flower-Feather Clan's elite flying squad of Qucusaur riders once patrolled all of Natlan, and Chasca says their pride borders on arrogance. To join, a warrior must master the skills and win the Qucusaurs' approval; even Chasca had to. Those who fail repeatedly and give up are the "Wingless", still prized warriors whom the clan quietly watches over. In 5.2 she kept watch over the failed applicant Coyllur. She saw through the Traveler's Saurian Indwelling stunt to cheer her up, because the "Qucusaur" moved like the Traveler, and whistled to cover their escape. When Phlogiston Wings arrived she argued for new trial standards for wing users rather than judging them by the old rules.

11.comment: Chasca: Ineffa and The Journey Home
11.content: In 5.8, Chasca found the unconscious automaton Ineffa on a beach near the clan, carrying a cryptex meant for the Traveler, and brought her to Xilonen. She offered the Nod-Krai caravan, including Zhuoxin and his family, shelter in her tribe. She kept asking Ineffa what "home" meant, and gave her own answer: somewhere you can always return, where someone waits, and "who says you can't have more than one home?" She told the legend of Lianca. When Citlali suggested Ineffa's core might be the hostile Eleventh Sovereign Lord, Chasca saw through the act. She said no one had given up on her and she would not give up on Ineffa, and if needed "we defeat her". Zhuoxin was revealed to have worked for the Fatui and a "Marionette"-led regiment was found in the old Lords' territory; she still welcomed his family, "old enemies, turned new friends".

12.comment: Chasca: Lianca and the founding of the clan
12.content: Chasca tells Lianca's story as the clan's origin. Lianca was raised by a dragon mother who sent her out to find her own path. She settled disputes between humans and Saurians without regard to old grudges, protected the weak from the strong, and gathered a community of people and Saurians united by freedom and equality. She was "the uncrowned queen". She was the first bearer of Vuka. In 5.8 she heard Citlali's account that Lianca's surrogate mother was the Eighth of the Thirteen Sovereign Lords, said (perhaps only in legend) to have been "executed" by a curse from another sovereign ruler for her pro-human sympathies. Chasca suspects the other rulers simply did not trust her. The parallel to her own Peacemaker work is not lost on her.

13.content: Chasca rejects comparisons between them: if the Pilgrimage were a tree and she a vulture on its highest branch, Mavuika would be the sun, "the champion of an entire era". Being high up only shows her how high she wants to fly. During the 5.0 crisis she told Paimon that Mavuika could handle anything. Mavuika calls Chasca's survival a miracle and wants to make Natlan "gentler", because even the strongest need a break. After the war Mavuika apologised for Chuychu's death and visited Chasca's parents, and she told Chasca her mother was worried about her safety.

14.content: When Chasca was small, the most learned elders of Natlan gathered to debate how to manage her condition. Citlali slipped out, came back with food and wine, and ate in front of them until the room fell silent. In 5.8 Chasca reminded her that she did not give up on her as a child. Ifa, the clan's Saurian vet, often discussed medicine with Chuychu and Cusco. After the coup Chasca rushed Coya to him; he glanced at her, said Cusco could handle it, and left. Chasca admits she was "just worrying too much".

15.content: Kinich: she first assumed Ajaw was a Saurian he treated like family, and learned how wrong that was; she envies Ajaw's command of human speech. Iansan: rare in being good at training both herself and others; Chasca wishes she taught flying. Ororon admires her "armed deterrence". In Mavuika's story quest (5.3), when Mavuika relayed Xbalanque's lesson that strength of mind matters as much as strength of body, Chasca nominated Kinich, the winner of the first peacetime Pilgrimage, and the gathering toasted him.

16.content: In 5.8 Chasca joined Mualani, the Traveler, Paimon and Mondstadt's Bennett (later Venti) on a trial-run holiday at the Easybreeze Holiday Resort. Ifa and Ororon also attended. She tested the paintball attractions at Wavey Bay and noticed the resort's tired Saurian staff. She pried gently into the trouble behind the scenes, and admired Bennett for going back out after every failure. Her wish at the resort: that her family stay safe and war leave Natlan for good.

17.comment: Chasca: Tournament of Glory in Bloom (5.5 event)
17.content: During a limited-time 5.5 event, Mavuika revived the old Bloomflower Trials in a new form. Chasca's team lost the first half to the Traveler, Kinich and Mualani. After learning of the bitter feud behind the original trials, she said not even a Peacemaker could have mediated clashes between whole tribes. When the others planned a staged quarrel as a ruse, she volunteered for clean-up instead, because if she saw them arguing she "wouldn't be able to resist stepping in". In the second half the Traveler joined her side, and they helped the ghost Antu find peace. Her verdict: "Finally, a few days off". People rarely quarrel right after big contests.

18.content: During the limited-time 6.5 event Where Waves Meet the Reef, clan members brought word from Nod-Krai that someone was selling "Wayob fragments" at Nasha Town's trade expo. Chasca brought Citlali to investigate. She reminded Citlali that the organisers protected the merchants and that confronting the seller would cause more trouble than it solved. The seller was Nkrumah of the Masters of the Night-Wind. With the Traveler mediating, Citlali let him stay until the expo ended, warning that he would answer to Biram afterwards.

19.comment: Chasca: Fontaine wargame with Chevreuse (6.7 event)
19.content: During the limited-time 6.7 event Final Long-Range Sightlines, Chasca flew to Fontaine for a wargame. She strayed near a Special Patrol range and was fired on twice as an "airborne target", but was too fast to hit, and Chevreuse called it off and apologised. She was impressed by the Patrol's discipline. She concluded that when individuals lack overwhelming strength, cooperation and discipline guarantee combat power, and that her clan's weak spot is absorbing losses and training efficiently. She half-joked about poaching Chevreuse, then conceded Fontaine would never let her go. The two agreed on an exchange; Chasca picked Zhunan and Inkanak to send. She found the stone-walled city surprisingly comforting.

20.content: Chasca chose her adoption day, 10 December, as her birthday at her family's suggestion. Since the war she wants to share it with friends as well as family, over grilled meat and fish by a bonfire. As a birthday gift she hands over a gun loaded with six rounds: one is her best home-made whistling firework, the other five earlier trial runs. She promises six perfect rounds next year. Her specialty dish, Moment of Respite, comes from cooking Surf, Turf, and Perch.
